title: GTA 6 Sales: $3.79 Billion Day One, Bugs and Who Beat It First
description: GTA 6 sold 32.5M copies before launch and made $3.79B on day one. Full sales breakdown, launch glitches, and the streamers who beat it first.
excerpt: Record sales, a 39-hour speedrun from New Zealand and a list of very GTA glitches. Everything that happened in GTA 6's first five days, with the numbers checked.
heroAlt: Neon bar chart comparing GTA V's day-one revenue with GTA 6's record $3.79 billion launch
intro: Grand Theft Auto VI has been out for less than a week and it has already rewritten the record books. Rockstar's return to Vice City launched on 19 November 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, and within 24 hours Take-Two announced the biggest opening in entertainment history. At the same time, streamers were racing each other to the credits, and players were filling social media with clips of cars flying into orbit.

In this guide we break down the real GTA 6 sales numbers (and which figures are official versus estimates), how much money GTA 6 made compared with GTA V, which streamers finished the game first and how long it took them, and the bugs and glitches players have reported so far. Every number below comes from a named source, listed at the bottom of the page, because a lot of what is circulating online right now is guesswork.

sections.heading: GTA 6 sales at a glance
paragraphs: If you only want the headline numbers, here they are. These are the figures that matter as of 23 November 2026, five days after launch.
list: 32.5 million copies sold before release, according to Take-Two (official, announced 20 November 2026)
About $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide (official company estimate, including pre-sales)
About 24.5 million pre-orders and $2.36 billion in revenue on PlayStation and Xbox (Sensor Tower estimate, not official)
Roughly 11.2 million copies and $815.7 million in GTA V's first 24 hours back in 2013, for comparison
A Metascore of 99, tying the highest score Metacritic has ever recorded
39 hours 38 minutes: the first reported completion, by New Zealand streamer BrycexD

sections.heading: How many copies has GTA 6 sold?
paragraphs: The only official number so far comes from Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company. On 20 November 2026 it announced that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million units before release, which it called a new record across all platforms. That is pre-release sales alone, so the real total by the end of launch week will be higher. Take-Two has not yet published a running total for copies sold after launch day.

To put 32.5 million in context, GTA V sold about 11.2 million copies in its first 24 hours in 2013, which earned it a Guinness World Record at the time. GTA 6 nearly tripled that before a single disc reached a console. GTA V went on to sell more than 200 million copies over the following decade, which shows how much room there is for GTA 6 to keep growing.

There are also third-party estimates. Market intelligence firm [Sensor Tower estimated](https://www.videogameschronicle.com/news/gta-6-sold-around-25-million-copies-and-made-2-36-billion-in-its-first-day-estimates-suggest/) around 24.5 million pre-orders across PlayStation and Xbox. The gap between that and Take-Two's 32.5 million is mostly because Sensor Tower only tracks digital storefronts on two platforms, while Take-Two counts every sale, physical copies included. When you see two different GTA 6 copies-sold figures online, that difference is usually why.

Prediction markets expect the climb to continue. One report noted that traders on Kalshi priced in an 86% chance that Take-Two will report at least 50 million copies sold before 1 March 2027. That is a market's guess, not a sales result, but it gives a sense of where the industry expects GTA 6 to land by its first quarterly report.

sections.heading: How much money did GTA 6 make? The $3.79 billion first day
paragraphs: Take-Two put GTA 6's day-one retail sales at approximately $3.79 billion worldwide. The footnote matters here: it is a company estimate through the end of 19 November, and it includes all the pre-sales made in the months before launch. It is a retail sales figure, not profit, and it has not been audited. Still, no film, album or game has ever announced a bigger opening.

CNBC calculated that $3.79 billion is nearly five times the roughly $800 million GTA V made on its first day. Part of that jump is simple price inflation: GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition, while GTA V launched at $59.99. Most of it is pure demand, though. Thirteen years of waiting, two delays and the best reviews in the series' history created a launch that was always going to be enormous.

Sensor Tower's lower estimate of $2.36 billion tells an interesting story on its own. According to that data, PlayStation accounted for about 75% of the pre-order revenue it tracked, and around 82% of pre-orders were for the more expensive $100 Ultimate Edition. In other words, players were not just buying GTA 6. Most of them bought the most expensive version on day one. If you are still deciding which edition to get, our [GTA 6 buyer's guide](/blog/gta-6-buyers-guide-price-editions-size) explains exactly what the extra $20 gets you.

sections.heading: GTA 6 vs GTA V: launch numbers compared
paragraphs: Comparing the two launches side by side shows just how much bigger GTA 6 is, even after you allow for higher prices and a larger console audience.

One thing GTA 6 does not have at launch is a PC version, which makes its numbers even more impressive. Every sale so far has come from just two console families. GTA V also launched on consoles only, but it was available on older PS3 and Xbox 360 hardware with a far bigger installed base. GTA 6 skipped the PS4 and Xbox One entirely, and still sold almost three times as many copies before launch.
list: Day-one revenue: about $815.7 million for GTA V (2013) vs about $3.79 billion for GTA 6 (2026, includes pre-sales)
Early copies: about 11.2 million in 24 hours for GTA V vs 32.5 million pre-release for GTA 6
Launch price: $59.99 for GTA V vs $79.99 Standard and $99.99 Ultimate for GTA 6
Launch platforms: PS3 and Xbox 360 for GTA V vs PS5 and Xbox Series X|S for GTA 6, with no PC version for either at launch
Review score: 97 on Metacritic for GTA V vs a record-tying 99 for GTA 6

sections.heading: Who was the first person to beat GTA 6?
paragraphs: The race to the credits started the moment the game unlocked, and it was won from the other side of the world. New Zealand streamer BrycexD is [widely reported](https://powerupgaming.co.uk/2026/11/20/brycexd-and-ishowspeed-become-the-first-streamers-to-complete-gta-6/) as the first person to beat GTA 6's story. The timer in his screenshot read 39 hours, 38 minutes and 22 seconds, less than two days after the game came out. He said he stayed awake for more than 50 hours with no proper breaks, and his stream peaked at around 14,000 viewers across the platforms he was broadcasting on.

Time zones gave him a real head start. Because the game unlocked at midnight local time, players in New Zealand got access hours before the United States and most of Europe. BrycexD also said he had no idea what happens in the story and planned to replay it properly, which tells you how fast he was moving.

In second place was one of the biggest names in streaming, iShowSpeed. He began playing at midnight, a couple of hours before the US launch, and reportedly reached more than 80% of the story by the 40-hour mark. He finished in about 52 hours and 30 minutes, and clips of him reacting emotionally to the ending spread quickly across social media.

A word of caution before you go looking for those clips: the ending is a major spoiler, and plenty of fans have complained about finding it in their feeds. Rockstar has not confirmed any official completion order, and these times come from the streamers' own broadcasts and the outlets that covered them, so treat them as reported rather than verified.

sections.heading: How long does it take to beat GTA 6?
paragraphs: Those streamer marathons are not a fair guide for normal players. Both BrycexD and iShowSpeed were rushing the main missions and skipping almost everything optional. For a regular playthrough, the most cited figure comes from Rockstar itself: Rob Nelson, co-studio head at Rockstar North, [said it takes around 80 hours](https://www.gamesradar.com/games/grand-theft-auto/how-long-is-gta-6-about-80-hours-according-to-one-rockstar-devs-playthrough/) to beat GTA 6, although that run included some optional story content as well as the main missions.

Other estimates put the main story alone at roughly 50 to 70 hours, depending on how much you explore. One early player report put a full story run, with optional quests and every cutscene, at about 70 hours. Completionists chasing the Platinum trophy or every achievement should expect around 200 hours. For comparison, GTA V's main story took about 32 hours, so GTA 6 is easily the longest game Rockstar has made in the series. Want to know where all those hours go? Our [GTA 6 map guide](/blog/gta-6-map-leonida-vice-city-guide) covers every region of Leonida.

sections.heading: GTA 6 glitches and bugs players have found
paragraphs: No open world this big launches without problems, and GTA 6 is no exception. The good news is that most of what players are reporting are funny physics glitches rather than game-breaking disasters. Outlets including [PC Guide](https://www.pcguide.com/news/gta-6-bugs-draw-comparisons-to-cyberpunk-2077s-messy-launch-but-its-far-from-the-same-thing/) have pushed back on comparisons with Cyberpunk 2077's famously broken launch, pointing out that most players are not running into serious issues.
Here are the GTA 6 bugs and glitches that have been reported most often in the first few days:
list: Physics glitches: vehicles launching into the air after collisions, aircraft passing straight through buildings, and NPCs swimming sideways
Falling through the map: players clipping under the world, including Lucia dropping through the ground during a mission
Police encounter clipping: characters overlapping each other and passing through furniture during arrests
Mission softlocks: at least one player reported getting stuck in an early Lucia mission after leaving a bank, unable to progress
Crashes: reports of repeated crashes and freezes during the opening prologue
Wanted level stuck: some players say a wanted level refused to clear for hours
Xbox Series S textures: missing or low-resolution textures reported mostly on the cheaper Series S
Performance: some concerns about frame-rate stability on the base PS5, and a temporary network error on Xbox at launch

sections.heading: Is there a GTA 6 money glitch?
paragraphs: Not one that anyone has verified. Money glitch videos always appear within days of a GTA launch, and GTA 6 is no different, but no version-tested unlimited money glitch has been confirmed so far, and one guide specifically advises treating those claims as unverified. Be careful with videos that ask you to download files or visit outside websites to get free cash. Those are a common way to spread malware and steal accounts.

You may also see a claim that GTA 6 has two million bugs. That number is a pre-launch estimate based on Rockstar's older games, not a real count of problems in the finished game. It is a good example of how quickly made-up statistics spread during a big launch.

sections.heading: Has Rockstar patched GTA 6 yet?
paragraphs: As of 23 November 2026 we have not found official patch notes for GTA 6. Rockstar usually fixes the most common crashes and progression bugs in the first few weeks, and on consoles those updates download automatically. If you hit a crash or a mission that will not progress, the safest steps are to keep your console's system software up to date, leave automatic game updates switched on, and reload an earlier save rather than replaying the same checkpoint.

For confirmed fixes, check [Rockstar Support](https://support.rockstargames.com/) directly rather than relying on social media posts. We will update this article when the first official patch notes are published.

sections.heading: What GTA 6's record launch means for gaming
paragraphs: GTA 6's launch is a reminder that a single game can still dominate entertainment. It outsold every film opening ever recorded, it pulled huge audiences to streaming platforms before it was even released, and it did it on consoles alone. A PC version will almost certainly add another wave of sales when it arrives, as happened with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2.

The big questions now are how fast GTA 6 reaches 50 million copies, when Rockstar adds an online mode, and whether a 60fps option ever arrives on consoles. If you want the critics' verdict on the game itself, read our [GTA 6 review roundup](/blog/gta-6-review-roundup-metacritic).

Waiting for a 200 GB download, or taking a break after a 10-hour session? You can play a few quick free games right here on ClickVault. Drift Alley scratches the driving itch, Turf Takeover is a fast territory battle against five bots, and Tank Duel Arena is perfect for a few explosive rounds. If you would rather slow things down, try Checkmate Chess or browse every [free unblocked game](/games) on the site.

faq.q: How many copies has GTA 6 sold?
faq.a: Take-Two announced on 20 November 2026 that GTA 6 sold 32.5 million copies before release. An official total including launch-week sales has not been published yet.

faq.q: How much money did GTA 6 make on day one?
faq.a: Take-Two estimates about $3.79 billion in day-one retail sales worldwide, including pre-sales. That is nearly five times GTA V's roughly $800 million first day in 2013.

faq.q: Who was the first person to beat GTA 6?
faq.a: New Zealand streamer BrycexD is widely reported as first, finishing the story in 39 hours and 38 minutes. iShowSpeed was second at about 52 hours and 30 minutes.

faq.q: How long does it take to beat GTA 6?
faq.a: Rockstar North's co-studio head said around 80 hours including some optional story content. The main story alone takes most players about 50 to 70 hours, and 100% completion takes around 200 hours.

faq.q: Does GTA 6 have a lot of bugs?
faq.a: Players have reported physics glitches, clipping under the map, some mission softlocks and crashes, but most outlets say the launch is far smoother than Cyberpunk 2077's and that most players are not affected.

faq.q: Is there a GTA 6 money glitch?
faq.a: No verified money glitch has been confirmed so far. Avoid videos that ask you to download files or visit outside sites for free money, as these are often scams.

title: GTA 6 Reviews Are In: Metacritic Score, Praise, Complaints and Is It Worth It?
description: GTA 6 launched with a record-tying 99 on Metacritic. Here's what critics loved, what they didn't, how it runs on PS5 and Xbox, and whether it's worth $80.
excerpt: Thirteen years after GTA V, Rockstar's return to Vice City has landed with a record-tying 99 on Metacritic. Here is what that score actually means for you.
heroAlt: Illustration of a neon Vice City skyline at sunset with palm trees
intro: So it finally happened. After two delays, a mountain of rumours and more than a decade of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI launched on 19 November 2026 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. And if you were worried the game could never live up to the hype, the critics have a pretty clear answer for you.

GTA 6 opened with a 99 on Metacritic, which ties the highest score the site has ever recorded. That puts it level with The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, the game that has sat at the top of that list for more than twenty-five years. We read through the major reviews so you don't have to. Below you'll find what reviewers loved, the handful of complaints that kept coming up, how the game runs, and our honest take on whether it deserves your $80.

sections.heading: The GTA 6 Metacritic score, explained
paragraphs: When the review embargo lifted on 18 November, the PlayStation 5 version settled at 99 out of 100 from well over a hundred critic reviews, and there wasn't a single mixed or negative verdict among them. The Xbox Series X version showed the same score, although it was based on far fewer reviews at the time. OpenCritic, the other major aggregator, landed in the same 98 to 99 range with close to every critic recommending it.

It's worth pausing on how unusual that is. A 99 on its own is rare, but a 99 built from more than a hundred reviews is a different thing entirely. Ocarina of Time earned its score from a couple of dozen reviews in 1998, so GTA 6 reached the same number with roughly seven times as many critics weighing in. Before this week, the series record belonged to GTA IV at 98.
Big outlets including IGN, GameSpot, Eurogamer and GamesRadar+ all gave it perfect marks. The lowest scores we spotted were still around 90, which most games would happily frame and hang on the wall.

sections.heading: What critics loved about GTA 6
paragraphs: Reading review after review, a few themes come up again and again. The first is the world itself. Leonida, Rockstar's take on Florida, is described as the densest and most alive open world the studio has ever built. Reviewers keep mentioning the little things: people reacting to what you do, traffic that feels purposeful, and a Vice City that looks completely different at 3am than it does at noon.

The second is the story. GTA 6 follows Jason and Lucia, a couple pulled into a criminal conspiracy that spreads across the whole state. Many critics said this is the most emotionally grounded story the series has told, and that the relationship at its centre gives the chaos a heart that GTA V's three-way split sometimes lacked. Lucia, the first female lead in a mainline GTA in decades, gets particular praise.

Third, the sheer craft. Animation, lighting, weather and the way cars handle all came in for specific compliments. Several reviewers compared exploring the swamps and keys to Red Dead Redemption 2's wilderness, which is high praise given how highly regarded that game is.
list: A huge, detailed open world that feels lived in rather than just big
A more personal, character-driven story centred on Jason and Lucia
Some of the best visuals and animation on current consoles
Plenty of side activities spread across the whole of Leonida, not just Vice City

sections.heading: The complaints: 30fps and pacing
paragraphs: No game is perfect, and even a 99 comes with caveats. The criticism that showed up most often was performance. Rockstar confirmed before launch that GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on every console, including the PS5 Pro. The Pro version gets sharper image quality and better ray tracing, but not a higher frame rate. Rockstar has said that a 60fps build was tested and that hitting it meant stripping out much of the traffic and crowds that make the world feel busy.

For most players the game holds that 30fps target well, and reviewers generally said it felt smooth enough in practice. If you've been spoiled by 60fps shooters, though, you'll notice the difference, especially when driving fast. Rockstar's previous games received later updates, so a higher frame rate option isn't impossible down the line, but there's no promise of one.

The other recurring note was pacing in the later part of the story. A number of critics felt that the back half has a stretch that drags a little before the finale picks things back up. Again, this was described as a minor issue, not something that ruins the experience.

sections.heading: How big is the download?
paragraphs: Clear some space before you buy. The PS5 pre-load came in at roughly 210 GB, which makes GTA 6 one of the largest console downloads ever. Even the physical version contains a download code rather than the full game on disc, so you'll need both the storage and a decent internet connection on day one.
If your console is nearly full, now's a good time to uninstall a couple of big games you aren't playing. An external SSD is worth considering if you regularly juggle large titles.

sections.heading: What about GTA Online and PC?
paragraphs: Two things GTA 6 does not include at launch are a new online mode and a PC version. Rockstar describes the launch game as a single-player experience, and there's been no official word yet on when or how an online component will arrive. The existing GTA Online for GTA V continues to run alongside it.

PC players will have to keep waiting. Rockstar hasn't announced a PC release date, and judging by how GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 were handled, a PC version will most likely arrive later as its own release.

sections.heading: How GTA 6 compares with GTA V
paragraphs: GTA V came out in 2013 and went on to become one of the best-selling entertainment products of all time, so the comparison was always going to be unavoidable. Where GTA V split its story across three very different men and leaned hard on satire, GTA 6 narrows its focus to two people and a relationship. Critics say that makes the story feel more personal, even when the action gets just as outrageous as you'd expect from the series.

The world is the other big leap. GTA V's San Andreas was impressive for its time, but much of its countryside was empty space between points of interest. Leonida is described as being much busier, with several properly developed regions instead of one city and a lot of hills. It also reflects how much has changed in thirteen years: social media, viral videos and influencer culture are all part of the satire this time around.

sections.heading: Who should wait before buying?
paragraphs: Despite the glowing reviews, there are a few groups who might want to hold off. If you only play on PC, there's simply no version for you yet. If you hate 30fps games, it may be worth watching some gameplay first to see whether it bothers you. And if you mainly played GTA V for the online mode, remember that GTA 6 launches as a single-player game, with no new online mode at release.
Everyone else? There's very little reason to wait, especially as anyone who buys before 20 November also gets the Vintage Vice City Pack of bonus items.

sections.heading: Is GTA 6 worth $80?
paragraphs: GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition, which adds extra single-player cosmetics and vehicles. That's $10 more than the usual price for big console games, and it's fair to be annoyed about that.

Here's the thing, though. Based on what reviewers are saying about the size of the world and the length of the story, this is likely to be a game you play for a hundred hours or more. Measured by hours of entertainment per dollar, few games come close. If you own a PS5 or Xbox Series X|S and you enjoy open-world games even a little, the consensus is that GTA 6 is worth the money.
If you're on the fence, the Standard Edition is all you need. The Ultimate Edition content is cosmetic and can be bought as an upgrade later, so there's no pressure to pay the extra $20 up front.

sections.heading: Our verdict
paragraphs: It's rare for a game this hyped to land this well. The 30fps cap and a slightly slow patch in the story are real drawbacks, but they're small next to what critics describe as Rockstar's best world and most human story to date. If you've been waiting since 2013, the wait looks to have been worth it.

Waiting for your download to finish? While those 200-plus gigabytes come down, you can kill some time with a few quick browser games right here on ClickVault. Drift Alley scratches the driving itch, Tank Wars is great for a few explosive rounds, and Chicken Road Cross is a surprisingly tense lesson in crossing the street, which is more than most GTA characters ever learn.

faq.q: What is GTA 6's Metacritic score?
faq.a: GTA 6 launched with a Metascore of 99 on PS5, tying The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for the highest score in Metacritic's history.

faq.q: Does GTA 6 run at 60fps?
faq.a: No. Rockstar confirmed GTA 6 targets 30fps on PS5, PS5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S. The PS5 Pro improves image quality and ray tracing rather than frame rate.

faq.q: Is GTA 6 on PC?
faq.a: Not yet. GTA 6 launched on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S only, and Rockstar has not announced a PC release date.

faq.q: How much does GTA 6 cost?
faq.a: The Standard Edition is $79.99 and the Ultimate Edition is $99.99.

author: ClickVault Editorial

title: GTA 6 Map Guide: Vice City, Leonida and Every Region Explained
description: A clear guide to the GTA 6 map: how big Leonida is, what's in Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga.
excerpt: Leonida is the biggest world Rockstar has ever built. Here's a region-by-region tour of the GTA 6 map and how it compares with GTA V.
heroAlt: Illustrated map of Leonida showing Vice City, Ambrosia, Grassrivers, Mount Kalaga and Port Gellhorn
intro: Every Grand Theft Auto lives or dies by its map, and GTA 6 has the most ambitious one Rockstar has ever made. Instead of a single city with some countryside tacked on, the game takes place across Leonida, a fictional state modelled closely on Florida, with a modern-day Vice City at its heart.

If you've just started playing, or you're still deciding whether to pick it up, this guide walks you through the map region by region. We'll cover how big it is compared with GTA V, what each area is based on in real life, and what kind of experience each part of Leonida offers. We've avoided story spoilers, so it's safe to read before you play.

sections.heading: How big is the GTA 6 map?
paragraphs: Rockstar has described Leonida as roughly twice the size of GTA V's map. Rockstar North's Rob Nelson has also said that Vice City alone is about double the size of Los Santos, and that the built-up areas outside the city are many times larger than anything outside the city in GTA V. Fan estimates that try to measure the map put it somewhere around 120 to 160 square kilometres, though those are community calculations rather than official figures.

Raw size isn't really the headline, though. GTA V's map was big, but a lot of its countryside was empty hills and desert. Leonida is designed to feel like a real state, with several developed regions, smaller towns, islands, wetlands and wilderness. You'll have reasons to spend real time well outside Vice City, which wasn't always true in Los Santos.

sections.heading: Vice City: the neon heart of Leonida
paragraphs: Vice City is Rockstar's version of Miami, and it's where most players will spend their first hours. This isn't the pastel 1980s Vice City of the 2002 game. It's a modern city of glass towers, art deco beachfronts, canals and late-night strips, with a busy cruise port and a skyline that looks spectacular across the bay at sunset.

Expect beaches modelled on South Beach, a downtown business district, wealthy island neighbourhoods, a metro system, sports stadiums and plenty of nightlife. The water matters here too: jet skis and boats are a big part of getting around, and the ocean is full of marine life.
list: Inspired by: Miami and Miami Beach
Best for: nightlife, shopping, beaches and the busiest streets
Look out for: the causeways into downtown and the cruise-ship port

sections.heading: Why Rockstar went back to Vice City
paragraphs: Vice City has a special place in the series' history. The 2002 original, set in a neon-soaked 1980s version of Miami, is still one of the most beloved entries, and its soundtrack and style are a big part of why so many people fell for GTA in the first place. Bringing the city back in a modern setting lets Rockstar play with that nostalgia while saying something about the present day.

Florida is also perfect material for a series built on satire. Its mix of wealth and chaos, glamour and swamp, and its endless stream of viral headlines gives Rockstar a lot to work with. It's no surprise that the trailers leaned so heavily on social media clips and strange local news, because that's the tone the whole map is built around.

sections.heading: Leonida Keys: island hopping in the south
paragraphs: Stretching south of Vice City is a long chain of tropical islands linked by bridges, based on the real Florida Keys. This is where Jason and Lucia's story begins, so it's one of the first places you'll get to know.

The Keys have a slower, sun-bleached feel compared with the city. Long drives across open water, small marinas, bars and boats give it a holiday-postcard look, with just enough grime underneath to remind you this is still GTA.

sections.heading: Grassrivers: the swamp
paragraphs: West of the city lies Grassrivers, Leonida's take on the Everglades. It's a vast wetland of sawgrass, channels and mangroves, and it introduces airboats as a proper vehicle type for skimming across shallow water.

This is one of the areas reviewers single out for its atmosphere. Wildlife, including the alligators that appeared in the trailers, is part of the experience, and the region feels genuinely wild compared with the polished city just a short drive away.

sections.heading: Port Gellhorn: the forgotten coast
paragraphs: Further north and west, Port Gellhorn is a run-down coastal town inspired by Florida's Gulf Coast and Panhandle areas. Think faded motels, strip clubs, old industry and a sense that the good times passed through a long time ago.

Port Gellhorn gives GTA 6 a completely different tone from Vice City. It's where the game's satire turns towards small-town life, and it's a good reminder that Leonida isn't just one big glamorous city.

sections.heading: Ambrosia: farmland and industry
paragraphs: Inland, around the large lake in the middle of the state, you'll find Ambrosia. It's an agricultural and industrial region known for sugar production, with refineries, fields, rural roads and small communities.

Ambrosia is the quieter heartland of the map, and it's ideal for long drives, back-road chases and the kind of off-the-beaten-path side content Rockstar loves to hide in places most players race straight through.

sections.heading: Mount Kalaga: the great outdoors
paragraphs: In the north is Mount Kalaga National Park, Leonida's wilderness region. Forests, rivers, trails and campgrounds make this the most natural, Red Dead-like part of the map.
If you enjoy hunting, off-road driving or just exploring for the sake of it, Mount Kalaga is where you'll want to head once you've had your fill of the city.

sections.heading: Tips for exploring Leonida
paragraphs: With a map this large, a little planning goes a long way. Here are a few simple habits that will help you get more out of it:
list: Don't rush the main story; side activities are spread across the whole state
Use boats in Vice City and the Keys, as the water is often faster than the roads
Visit the same place at different times of day, since many areas change after dark
Try driving between regions at least once instead of always fast-travelling
Keep an eye out for garages you can buy; Jason and Lucia are often on the move, so where they live changes as the story goes on

sections.heading: Getting around Leonida
paragraphs: A bigger map means travel matters more, and Rockstar has given you plenty of options. Cars are still the main way to get around, with the series' usual mix of sports cars, family sedans, pickups and motorbikes. In the south, boats and jet skis are often quicker than the roads, especially for hopping between Vice City's islands and along the Keys.

Grassrivers adds airboats, which are built for shallow swamp water where normal boats struggle. The way each region favours a different type of vehicle is part of what makes the map feel varied: you'll drive differently in the city, on the long bridges of the Keys and on the dirt roads of Ambrosia.

sections.heading: How Leonida mirrors real Florida
paragraphs: Part of the fun of any GTA map is spotting the real places it's poking fun at. Vice City borrows heavily from Miami's skyline, beaches and nightlife. The Leonida Keys echo the Florida Keys and their famous Overseas Highway, Grassrivers is clearly the Everglades, and Port Gellhorn takes inspiration from the quieter, rougher towns of Florida's Gulf Coast.

Rockstar never copies a place street for street, though. Distances are shortened, landmarks are shuffled around and everything is exaggerated for the sake of gameplay and satire. Think of Leonida as Florida's greatest hits, compressed into something you can drive across in a single sitting.

sections.heading: Final thoughts
paragraphs: Leonida is the star of GTA 6 almost as much as Jason and Lucia are. From the neon of Vice City to the swamps of Grassrivers and the forests of Mount Kalaga, it's a map designed to be lived in rather than just driven across.

Need a break from all that driving? Try Drift Alley or Slope Runner X here on ClickVault for a quick hit of speed, or see how far you can get in Chicken Road Cross, where staying alive on the road is the whole point.

faq.q: Where is GTA 6 set?
faq.a: GTA 6 is set in Leonida, a fictional state based on Florida. Vice City, based on Miami, is its biggest city.

faq.q: How big is the GTA 6 map compared to GTA 5?
faq.a: Rockstar describes Leonida as roughly twice the size of GTA V's map, with Vice City alone about double the size of Los Santos.

faq.q: What regions are in GTA 6?
faq.a: The main regions are Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia and Mount Kalaga.

faq.q: Can you buy houses in GTA 6?
faq.a: Pre-release coverage indicates you can buy garages but not traditional safehouses, because Jason and Lucia's living situation changes as the story goes on.

title: GTA 6 Buyer's Guide: Price, Editions, Download Size and Performance
description: Everything to know before buying GTA 6: Standard vs Ultimate Edition, the Vintage Vice City Pack, the 210GB download, 30fps, PS5 Pro, Xbox and PC.
excerpt: Thinking about picking up GTA 6? Here's a plain-English guide to the editions, bonuses, storage you'll need and how it runs on each console.
heroAlt: Illustration of a games console, controller and an $80 price tag
intro: GTA 6 is out, it's scoring a perfect-looking 99 with critics, and you're probably wondering which version to buy and whether your console is ready for it. Rockstar hasn't made it complicated, but there are a few things that are easy to miss, like the bonus deadline and just how much storage you'll need.

This guide gathers everything in one place: the price of each edition, what the bonuses include, how big the download is, how the game performs on each console, and what's going on with PC and GTA Online. No spoilers, no fluff.

sections.heading: GTA 6 price: how much does it cost?
paragraphs: GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition in the US. Prices in other regions vary, so check your local PlayStation Store, Microsoft Store or the Rockstar Store for exact figures.

That $79.99 price is $10 higher than the $69.99 that most big console games have charged this generation, which caused plenty of grumbling when it was announced in June 2026. Still, it came in lower than some of the more dramatic rumours that suggested a $100 standard edition.

sections.heading: Standard vs Ultimate Edition: which should you buy?
paragraphs: Both editions contain the full game: the complete story with Jason and Lucia and the entire open world of Leonida. Nothing story-related is locked to the Ultimate Edition.

What the extra $20 gets you is a collection of bonus single-player content, such as additional vehicles, outfits, weapon finishes and other extras woven into the campaign. Some fans were unhappy about cosmetic content being placed behind a higher price in a single-player game, and that's a fair complaint. The good news is that the Ultimate content can be bought as an upgrade later, so you don't have to decide right now.
list: Choose Standard if you just want the game; you're not missing any story
Choose Ultimate if you love collecting cars and outfits and know you'll want them
Unsure? Buy Standard now and upgrade later if you change your mind

sections.heading: The Vintage Vice City Pack bonus (and its deadline)
paragraphs: Everyone who buys GTA 6 digitally before 20 November 2026, whether Standard or Ultimate, receives the Vintage Vice City Pack. Physical pre-orders get it too while stocks last. It's a nostalgic set of items inspired by the original 2002 Vice City, including a classic two-tone '55 Vapid Stanier with a garage, retro outfits and a weapon pattern that nods to Tommy Vercetti.

Digital pre-orders through the PlayStation Store and Microsoft Store also came with a free month of GTA+. If you want the Vintage Vice City Pack and haven't bought the game yet, don't wait: the deadline is the day after launch.

sections.heading: Download size: how much storage do you need?
paragraphs: This is the one that catches people out. The PS5 version of GTA 6 is roughly 210 GB. A standard PS5 has around 667 GB of usable space, so GTA 6 alone takes up close to a third of it.

Even buying a physical copy won't save the download, because the box contains a code rather than the full game. Before you buy, check your free space and clear room if needed. If you often juggle big games, an M.2 SSD on PS5 or an expansion card on Xbox Series X|S is a worthwhile upgrade.

sections.heading: Performance: 30fps on every console
paragraphs: Rockstar has confirmed that GTA 6 targets 30 frames per second on PS5, PS5 Pro, Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S. The game's huge amount of simulated traffic, pedestrians and detail is very demanding on the consoles' processors, and that's what limits the frame rate.

The PS5 Pro version is described as Pro Enhanced, using Sony's PSSR upscaling and improved ray tracing for a sharper, better-looking image. It doesn't get a 60fps mode. Rockstar has explained that a 60fps build was tested on the Pro, but reaching it meant removing much of the traffic and crowds that make the world feel alive.

Reviewers say the 30fps target is held well in practice. If you're particularly sensitive to frame rate, it's worth knowing in advance. Rockstar's past games have received updates after launch, but there's no confirmed plan for a higher frame rate mode.

sections.heading: PS5 or Xbox: which version is better?
paragraphs: Rockstar says the game plays best on PlayStation 5, pointing to DualSense haptic feedback, 3D audio and fast loading. In terms of frame rate, though, every console targets the same 30fps. The PS5 Pro offers the best image quality of the bunch.

In practice, the best version is the one on the console you already own. If you're buying a console specifically for GTA 6, the PS5 Pro is the premium choice, while the Xbox Series S is the budget option with lower resolution.

sections.heading: Is GTA 6 on PC?
paragraphs: Not at launch. GTA 6 is only available on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and Rockstar hasn't announced a PC release date. That matches what happened with GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2, which both arrived on PC well after their console launches.
If you're a PC-only player, there's no official timeline yet. Be wary of any website offering a GTA 6 PC download right now, because it isn't real and is very likely to be malware.

sections.heading: What about GTA Online?
paragraphs: Rockstar describes GTA 6 at launch as a single-player experience. There is no new online mode included at release, and Rockstar hasn't shared details of when or how a GTA 6 online component will arrive. The existing GTA Online for GTA V keeps running in the meantime.

sections.heading: Pre-loading and launch timing
paragraphs: If you bought the game digitally, pre-loading opened about a week before launch, so you could download most of the game ahead of time. The physical edition was released early on 12 November for the same reason. GTA 6 unlocked at midnight local time on 19 November, which meant players in New Zealand were the first in the world to start playing.
Buying now, after launch? Just start the download as early as you can and leave your console in rest mode overnight. Rest mode usually downloads faster than leaving the console on a busy home screen.

sections.heading: Digital or physical: which should you buy?
paragraphs: Normally a disc lets you skip a huge download and resell the game later. GTA 6 changes that maths, because the physical box contains a download code rather than the full game. That means you'll be downloading roughly the same amount of data either way.

The main reasons to choose physical are collecting the box and possibly finding a deal at a retailer. If you value convenience and want the game the moment you pay, digital is the simpler option. Either way, make sure your purchase lands before 20 November if you want the Vintage Vice City Pack, as physical copies only include it while stocks last.

sections.heading: Do you need a new TV or console?
paragraphs: You don't need anything special to enjoy GTA 6. A standard PS5 or Xbox Series X on a 4K TV will look great, and the Series S works fine on a 1080p or 1440p screen. HDR support on your TV helps bring out the neon of Vice City at night, but it isn't essential.

The PS5 Pro is the only upgrade that makes a visible difference, and even then it's sharper image quality rather than smoother motion. Unless you were already planning to upgrade, the console you have now is good enough.

sections.heading: Quick checklist before you buy
paragraphs: Run through this list and you'll be ready to play the moment your download finishes:
list: Pick your edition: Standard is enough for most players
Buy before 20 November if you want the Vintage Vice City Pack
Free up at least 210 GB of storage
Expect 30fps on every console, with the best image on PS5 Pro
Don't fall for 'GTA 6 PC download' scams

sections.heading: While you wait for the download
paragraphs: A 210 GB download can take a while on a normal connection. If you need something to pass the time, ClickVault has plenty of free browser games that load instantly. Try a few rounds of Tank Wars, hold the line in Tower Rush Defense, or see how high you can bounce in Sky Hopper.

faq.q: How much is GTA 6?
faq.a: GTA 6 costs $79.99 for the Standard Edition and $99.99 for the Ultimate Edition in the US.

faq.q: How big is the GTA 6 download?
faq.a: About 210 GB on PS5. The physical edition contains a download code, so you still need the storage space.

faq.q: What is in the GTA 6 Ultimate Edition?
faq.a: Extra single-player content such as vehicles, outfits and weapon finishes. The story and world are the same in both editions.

faq.q: When does the Vintage Vice City Pack deadline end?
faq.a: The pack is included with digital purchases made before 20 November 2026, and with physical pre-orders while stocks last.

title: What Is Prestige in Idle Games? When to Reset (Beginner's Guide)
description: Prestige resets explained simply: what prestige does in idle and clicker games, why resetting makes you faster, and exactly when to hit the button.
excerpt: Resetting all your progress on purpose sounds backwards. Here is why prestige is the most important button in any idle game — and how to know when to press it.
author: ClickVault Editorial
heroAlt: Illustration of idle game numbers growing after a prestige reset
keywords: what is prestige in idle games
intro: Almost every idle or clicker game eventually offers you a strange deal: give up everything you have built, and in return get a permanent bonus. This is called prestige, and it is the single biggest factor in how fast you progress.
This guide explains what prestige actually does, why it works, and a simple rule for deciding when to reset.

sections.heading: What prestige means in an idle game
paragraphs: Prestige is a voluntary reset. Your currency, producers and upgrades go back to zero, but you keep a permanent multiplier that boosts everything you earn in the next run. Different games give it different names — Franchise, Rebirth, New shaft, Jump system or Resonate — but the idea is always the same.
In the games on ClickVault, each prestige level adds a flat bonus to all income, and the amount you need to earn before the next prestige grows each time.

sections.heading: Why resetting makes you faster
paragraphs: Idle game costs grow exponentially: each extra producer costs a bit more than the last. Eventually your income cannot keep up and progress slows to a crawl. That slowdown is the signal.

After a prestige your multiplier lets you race back through the early game in a fraction of the time, and you end up further ahead than where you stopped. Players who never prestige usually stall; players who reset at the right moment keep accelerating.

sections.heading: When should you prestige?
paragraphs: A good rule of thumb is to reset when the next meaningful purchase would take you longer than it took to reach your current point after the last reset. In practice that usually means:
list: Your next producer or upgrade is more than a few minutes away.
You have unlocked the prestige button and the bonus is noticeably bigger than your current one.
Active clicking no longer makes a visible difference to your income.

sections.heading: Common prestige mistakes
paragraphs: The most common mistake is waiting too long. Holding on for one more upgrade can cost far more time than the reset would have saved. The second is resetting too early, before the bonus is large enough to matter.
Games with a low prestige bar, such as Crystal Tap Tycoon, are a great place to practise because you can reset several times in one session and feel the difference immediately.

faq.q: Do I lose everything when I prestige?
faq.a: You lose your current currency, producers and upgrades, but keep a permanent multiplier that makes every future run faster.

faq.q: Is it ever bad to prestige?
faq.a: Only if the bonus is too small to make up for the progress you give up. If the game shows the reward, reset once it clearly beats your current multiplier.

faq.q: Which ClickVault game is best for learning prestige?
faq.a: Crystal Tap Tycoon has the lowest prestige bar, so you can try several resets in a single short session.

We loaded every game below on a stock managed Chromebook with no extensions, no sideloading and no developer mode. If a game needed a plugin, a download or a login wall, it did not make the list.

sections.heading: What makes an idle game 'unblocked'
paragraphs: There is no such thing as a game that is universally unblocked. What people actually mean is a game that is delivered as plain HTML5 over HTTPS from a domain that has not been categorised as gaming by the network filter, and that does not need anything installed to run.
That gives you three practical requirements, and every entry on this list meets all three.
list: Runs entirely in the browser with HTML5 and WebGL, no Flash, Unity Web Player or Java applet.
Saves progress to local storage, so you keep your numbers even without an account.
Degrades gracefully on a low-spec machine with integrated graphics and 4 GB of RAM.

sections.heading: The best pure clickers
paragraphs: Pure clickers put the whole game in one number going up. The good ones make the first ten minutes feel generous and the next ten hours feel earned, usually by hiding a prestige multiplier behind a wall you can just about see from the start.

Cookie Empire Tycoon is the cleanest example we host. Your first upgrade costs fifteen cookies and arrives inside twenty seconds, which is exactly the kind of early payoff that makes the genre stick. Crystal Tap Tycoon is the opposite pitch: a deliberately tight thirty-minute prestige loop built for people who only get one free period.

sections.heading: The best idle games with real strategy
paragraphs: If a bare number going up does nothing for you, the management-flavoured end of the genre adds decisions with actual opportunity cost. Idle Space Colony makes you trade oxygen against power against population, and a bad allocation will stall you for twenty minutes.
Idle Mine Shaft sits in the middle. There is a genuine routing puzzle in how you sink shafts and staff elevators, but the game will still tick along happily if you ignore it for a day.

sections.heading: How offline earnings change what you should play
paragraphs: Offline earnings are the single biggest factor in whether an idle game suits a school day. A game that pays full rate while closed rewards checking in twice a day. A game that pays nothing while closed effectively demands a pinned tab.

Check the upgrade list for anything mentioning offline, away or absent production before you commit an afternoon. If it caps offline income at two hours, treat it as an active game with idle decoration.

sections.heading: Playing without wrecking your battery
paragraphs: Clicker games look cheap to run and often are not. An uncapped animation loop with a few hundred particle sprites will happily burn a Chromebook battery faster than a video call.

Two things help more than anything else: turn off particle effects in the options menu if the game exposes them, and keep the game in a foreground tab rather than a background one. Most browsers throttle background timers anyway, so a background idle tab is frequently earning less than you think while still costing you power.

faq.q: Do these games need Flash?

title: How Idle Games Work: Prestige, Offline Earnings & Game Math
description: Learn how idle games use geometric costs, prestige resets, offline earnings and multipliers—and how to spot when a game is stalling.
excerpt: Every idle game is the same three formulas wearing a different costume. Once you can see them, you can predict when a game is about to stall and when it is about to snowball.
author: ClickVault Editorial
intro: Idle games feel generous at the start and grinding later, and that shift is not an accident. It falls out of one design decision: costs grow geometrically while income grows linearly until you buy your way out of it.

Understanding the three formulas underneath the genre takes about ten minutes and permanently changes how you play. You stop buying the upgrade that is in front of you and start buying the one that resets the curve.

sections.heading: The cost curve is geometric, and that is the whole game
paragraphs: In nearly every idle game, the nth copy of a building costs base multiplied by growth raised to the power of n. Growth is usually somewhere between 1.07 and 1.15. At 1.15, every seventh purchase roughly triples the price.

Your income from that building, meanwhile, is flat per copy. Ten copies produce ten times one copy. So income climbs in a straight line while price climbs on a curve, and the curve always wins. Every stall you ever hit is that crossover point arriving.

sections.heading: Prestige exists to bend the curve, not to reward you
paragraphs: Prestige resets your buildings and hands back a permanent multiplier, usually scaled to the square root or cube root of your lifetime earnings. That sublinear scaling is deliberate: it means your second run is much faster than your first, but your tenth is not ten times faster than your ninth.

The practical rule most well-tuned games converge on is to reset when your multiplier would gain somewhere between fifty and one hundred per cent. Resetting earlier wastes the run-up; resetting later means grinding through the flat part of the curve for a rounding error.
list: Multiplier gain under 20 per cent: keep playing, you are leaving value on the table.
Multiplier gain 50 to 100 per cent: this is the sweet spot for almost every game in the genre.
Multiplier gain over 300 per cent: you waited too long and spent an hour earning nothing.

sections.heading: Offline earnings are a rate, a cap and a multiplier
paragraphs: Offline accrual has three separate knobs and games advertise only the flattering one. The rate is what fraction of your active income you earn while away, often 50 per cent. The cap is the maximum window that counts, often two to eight hours. The multiplier is whatever upgrade or advert doubles it.
A game paying 100 per cent with a two-hour cap is far worse for a school day than one paying 25 per cent with a twenty-four-hour cap. Always read for the cap first.

sections.heading: Why the numbers get silly on purpose
paragraphs: Once costs grow geometrically for long enough you run out of ordinary number names, which is why the genre is full of sextillions and why so many games switch to scientific notation past a certain tier.

This is not padding for its own sake. Very large numbers let a designer hand you an upgrade that multiplies income by a thousand and still have somewhere to go afterwards. The absurdity is the pressure valve that keeps the reward curve from flattening.

sections.heading: Spotting a badly tuned game in five minutes
paragraphs: Buy the cheapest producer repeatedly and watch how fast the price outruns your income. If you stall before your first upgrade unlocks, the growth exponent is set too high and the game is going to lean on advert-watching to unstick you.

The other reliable tell is an upgrade list with no visible next tier. Good idle games show you the locked thing you cannot afford yet, because the anticipation is the product. A game that hides its progression is usually hiding how little of it there is.

faq.q: Is clicking faster actually worth it?
faq.a: Only in the first few minutes. In almost every idle game, manual clicks stop mattering once your passive income passes roughly ten times your click value, which usually happens inside the first half hour.

faq.q: Should I always take the advert bonus?
faq.a: Take the ones that multiply income for a fixed window while you are actively playing. Skip the ones that grant a flat sum, because a flat reward that felt large an hour ago is a rounding error now.

faq.q: What does sublinear prestige scaling mean in practice?
faq.a: It means your multiplier grows more slowly than your earnings do. Earning a hundred times more in a run might only double your permanent bonus, which is what stops the genre from collapsing after three resets.

faq.q: Do idle games ever end?
faq.a: Most have a defined final upgrade and an ending screen, then continue in an endless mode. A minority are genuinely unbounded and simply keep adding zeroes.

title: Why School Networks Block Games, and What 'Unblocked' Really Means
description: A plain explanation of how school and office web filters categorise sites, why some browser games load and others do not, and what the term unblocked actually describes.
excerpt: Filters do not detect games. They match domains against a category list. Understanding that difference explains almost every case of one game loading and another not.
author: ClickVault Editorial
intro: The word unblocked has drifted a long way from anything technical. It started as a description of a specific situation and is now mostly a search term, which is why so many sites promising unblocked games do not load on the network you actually care about.
Here is what is really happening between your browser and the game, and why the answer is different on every network.

sections.heading: Filters match categories, not content
paragraphs: A school web filter almost never looks at what a page contains. It resolves the domain, looks it up in a commercial category database, and allows or denies based on whether that category is on the permit list. Games, streaming and social are the usual first three to go.

This is why a game can be entirely wholesome and still be blocked, and why a site with no games on it at all can be blocked for having once been categorised as gaming. The decision was made by a database, not by an assessment of the page.

sections.heading: Why one game loads and the next does not
paragraphs: Browser games are usually embedded from a different domain than the site you are looking at. The page is served from one host, the game itself from another. The filter sees both requests separately.

So a portal can load perfectly while every game on it shows a blank rectangle, because the page domain is uncategorised and the embed domain is not. That mismatch accounts for the large majority of broken embeds.
list: Page loads, game is blank: the embed host is filtered, not the site.
Nothing loads at all: the site domain itself is categorised and blocked.
Game loads then freezes: usually a WebGL or memory limit on a managed device, not the filter.

sections.heading: What unblocked honestly means
paragraphs: Used accurately, it means a game delivered from a domain that a given filter has not categorised as gaming, using only standard web technology so nothing needs installing. Both halves are conditional on the network.
No site can truthfully promise it is unblocked everywhere, ours included. A filter administrator can categorise any domain at any time, and a well-run network eventually will.

sections.heading: The part worth saying plainly
paragraphs: If your school or employer blocks games, that is a decision made by the people who own the network and the device. Working around it can breach an acceptable use policy, and on a managed device it can be logged in ways that are not obvious from the machine itself.

We are not going to publish proxy lists or filter-evasion instructions. What this site is for is playing browser games on a network where that is allowed: your own connection, your own laptop, a break at a place that does not mind.

sections.heading: Making the most of a restricted machine
paragraphs: Where games are permitted, a managed device is still a constrained one. Assume integrated graphics, limited memory and an aggressive tab-suspension policy, and prefer games that state a low system requirement.

Progress on almost every browser game is stored locally, so it lives on that specific device and profile. If administrators wipe profiles between terms, expect to start over, and treat any run you care about as something to finish rather than bank.

faq.q: Is it against the rules to play games at school?
faq.a: That depends entirely on your school's acceptable use policy. If games are blocked, it is safe to assume the policy discourages them, and the honest answer is to ask rather than to route around it.

faq.q: Why did a game that worked last week stop working?
faq.a: Most often the embed host was newly categorised by the filter vendor, which happens continuously. Less often, the game's own host changed domains.

faq.q: Do you provide proxies or filter workarounds?
faq.a: No. We host and link browser games for networks where that is permitted, and we do not publish anything intended to bypass a filter.

faq.q: Does incognito mode unblock anything?
faq.a: No. Network-level filtering happens between the device and the internet, so it applies identically in a private window. Incognito only affects what is stored locally, and it will also discard your game saves.
